transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because... even on my better days lately, I just can't shake this feeling that some of the people at my church are watching me. And the walking club, too. We usually walk on Tuesday mornings down by the lake, though last week it was just too muddy. I actually had to buy those new orthotic inserts for my sneakers because my knees just aren't what they used to be, you know? They charge an arm and a leg for them at the pharmacy down on Main Street. 

But anyway, I just know they're watching me, and they've started putting these little messages about me in the church bulletin. The bulletin is printed on this heavy cream paper now, the new secretary changed it last month. And it's not just the bulletin, it's in the things they say to each other when I'm around... just little hidden messages about me in their conversations. I really don't know why they'd do that, but it's why I came in.
Have you noticed any significant periods where your mood has been extremely low or unusually high, separate from these feelings of being watched?

Well, yes... I've been feeling just awfully low for a long time now. It's like this heavy blanket of sadness, and I feel guilty all the time, though I don't even know what for. I just don't care about things anymore. I used to love baking, you know. I made the best rhubarb pie for the church bake sale every spring. My mother taught me the recipe when I was just a girl, back when we lived in Ohio. We had this huge rhubarb patch behind the garage, and I'd go out with a butter knife to cut the stalks. You have to be careful with the leaves, though, because they're poisonous. I read an article in Reader's Digest once about a woman who made a salad with them and got terribly sick... 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. The sadness. It's just been there for most of this whole stretch. Even on the days when the... the messages in the bulletin or the whispering isn't as bad, or when I'm not feeling as suspicious of everyone. The sadness and the guilt, they just sit there in the background, all the time. It really takes it out of you. Speaking of taking it out of you, the price of groceries lately is just exhausting. Have you seen what they charge for a dozen eggs? It's highway robbery, it really is.
Looking back, did you experience these long periods of sadness and guilt before you first started noticing these messages and feeling watched, or did the feelings of being watched start first?

Well, let me think... the sadness definitely came first. I remember because it started right around the time I stopped going to my Tuesday morning water aerobics class, which was... oh, it's been about a year and two months now that I've had this deep sadness and guilt just sitting on my chest, and not caring about things. I used to love that water aerobics class. The instructor, Brenda, she had the brightest pink swimsuit you ever did see. It had these little ruffles along the top. She said she got it on clearance at the outlet mall off Interstate 95. Have you ever been to that outlet mall? It's huge, you could get lost in there. My sister went last Thanksgiving and couldn't find her car for two hours. 

But anyway, the sadness started about a year and two months ago, long before I started noticing the messages in the bulletin. The messages only started... well, I guess maybe a few months ago? But the heavy sadness, that's been dragging me down for over a year. It's funny how time just slips away when you're feeling like that, isn't it? Just like how fast the seasons change. The leaves are already starting to turn, and I haven't even put my patio furniture away yet. I usually have it all covered up by Labor Day.
Before this year-long period of sadness started, have you ever experienced a similar, long-lasting episode of such deep depression in your past?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I've had days where I felt a little blue, like anyone else, but nothing like this heavy, awful feeling that just won't leave me alone. Not for this long, anyway. It's funny, when I think about the past, I usually just remember the good times. Like when my husband and I took that trip to Mount Rushmore. Oh, that was back in '92, I think. We drove the whole way in our old Buick LeSabre. It was that awful beige color, you know the one? It looked like a giant stick of butter going down the highway. The air conditioning broke somewhere in South Dakota, and it was just sweltering. We had to roll all the windows down, and the wind just whipped my hair into a terrible knot. I had to buy a special detangling comb at a rest stop just to get a brush through it. They had the nicest little gift shop there, though. I bought a thimble with a jackalope painted on it for my collection. I have over two hundred thimbles now, you know. I keep them in a glass display case in the hallway... but no, I've never felt this kind of deep sadness before. Just the regular ups and downs of life until this started.
During the times when your mood has felt slightly better over the last few months, have you still felt that people were sending you hidden messages or watching you?

Well, yes, actually. There was this one spell, maybe for a few weeks, where I was actually feeling a little lighter. I was getting dressed every day, eating a bit better... I even made a pot roast one Sunday. I hadn't made a pot roast in ages. I use the chuck roast, you know, and I sear it in a cast-iron Dutch oven first. That's the secret to keeping the juices in. My grandmother gave me that Dutch oven when I got married. It weighs an absolute ton, I can barely lift it out of the bottom cabinet anymore. I have to get down on my hands and knees just to pull it out, and my knees just aren't what they used to be. I tried taking that glucosamine stuff they sell at the pharmacy, but the pills are so big I feel like I'm swallowing a horse pill. I don't know how anybody gets those down without choking. 

But, oh, what was I saying? Right, the messages. Yes, even during those few weeks when I wasn't feeling so terribly weighed down by the sadness, I still heard my name being whispered in the house when I was alone. And I still knew the people at church were hinting about me in the bulletin. It didn't stop just because I had a bit more energy to make dinner. It just kept right on going, like a leaky faucet you can't quite fix. Speaking of which, I really need to call the plumber about the sink in the guest bathroom. It drips all night long, just drip, drip, drip. It drives me absolutely up the wall.
